te: It launched a scheme to pay companies extra for making forty-one of these missing ingredients in India.
Nearly seven thousand crore rupees, set aside.
And one company took the biggest bet of all.
Kakinada, Andhra Pradesh.
On the coast, a new plant goes up, built by Aurobindo Pharma, through its unit called Lyfius.
Inside are the giant tanks I just told you about.
The company says it cost around two thousand five hundred crore rupees, and it's built to make fifteen thousand tonnes of penicillin G every year.
In twenty twenty-four, the tanks start running.
For the first time in more than ten years...
India is growing its own penicillin again.
But you know the trap.
Even with Indian penicillin ready, cheap imports were still waiting at the port.
So on the twenty-ninth of January, twenty twenty-six, the government stepped in.
It set a minimum price at the border.
If penicillin powder comes in cheaper than about two thousand two hundred rupees a kilo, it now needs a special licence.
The same rule covers amoxicillin and its base powder.
Think of it as a shield.
It gives the new Indian plant breathing room, while it grows big enough to stand on its own.
And in September twenty twenty-six, after the Kakinada plant complained, the government also started checking whether China is selling penicillin here below a fair price.
But that shield has an end date.
It runs for one year... until January twenty twenty-seven.
